svg.title: Layered Logic Mirror — Home/Controls screen wireframe
svg.desc: Lo-fi wireframe of the React Native Home/Controls screen in the Layered Logic Mirror app. Shows the resting state (Power button, full-width color wheel with corner preview and hex code display, 4 discrete brightness step buttons at 25/50/75/100, and a 7-pattern preset grid) with 6 numbered callouts pairing each UI decision to its source rationale. A 4-thumbnail strip below documents power-off, mid-color-drag, brightness-selected, and disconnected alternate states. Phone proportions match Pixel 9 (360x800 dp, 9:20 ratio). Brand indigo (#3214FF) marks active state and primary affordances.
svg.text: Layered Logic Mirror · App/v1 · Mobile (React Native, Pixel 9)
Mirrors the physical button's power gesture. Passive stakeholders
(housemates, guests) can find "off" without learning brightness
gestures. Tapping a color or pattern while off implicitly turns it
on (post-mini-sprint #3 fix) — wire state on/brightness coupled.
512×512 HSV polar wheel beats hex inputs or fixed swatches for
visual color picking. Magnifier bubble lifts above the finger so
the target color isn't covered. Scroll-locked during drag so the
Corner preview uses the wheel's negative space
Color preview sits at 45° from the wheel center, in the empty
corner outside the inscribed circle so it doesn't cover any
colors. Persistent during drag — pair with the magnifier for a
two-point read: where the finger is + what got committed.
Brightness: discrete steps, not a slider
4 buttons at 25/50/75/100 mirror the physical button's 4-step
brightness modality — unifies the mental model across hardware
and app. Also dodges the slider-flood failure (live-during-drag
10 msg/sec was the original surface of post-mini-sprint #1).
Patterns: ship-with preset grid (editor is V2)
7 patterns ship in firmware (solid, rainbow, scanner, spinner,
random, breathing, twinkle). Pattern editor — letting users define
new patterns from the app — is deferred to V2. V1 ships with what
the firmware supports; app maps 1:1 to firmware pattern_id.
Each pattern has its own buzz signature; brightness taps encode
the chosen value into the haptic intensity. Every action calls
haptic() + apply() on tap — no wait for state broadcast. The
authoritative broadcast settles the UI; haptic confirms the gesture.
LL-073 · App/v1/src/haptic.ts · post-mini-sprint bugfix UX polish
Power-off behavior, mid-interaction feedback, and connection-loss states the resting wireframe doesn't show.
Magnifier bubble floats above the finger
showing the color at the touch point.
Corner preview updates live; hex code
Haptic intensity scales with the step:
Find mirror in Settings to reconnect.
path. Controls remain visible but greyed.
Last-known state shown so the user can
see what was set when the link dropped.
